settings.title: Make it yours.
settings.about_body: FordCast checks Austin-area trips against crossing records, official reports and available creek readings. Four record links across two research corridors support a separate experimental gauge study. Road-flood prediction is unverified.
settings.privacy_body: Nearby crossing checks use your location on this device. Route planning sends start, destination and avoidance coordinates to the routing service; address search sends your query and nearby coordinates to the search provider. Launching Google Maps shares the route with Google. Saved crossings and settings stay on this device.
settings.review: Bilingual EN/ES strings verified for placeholder and safety-lexicon parity.
settings.sources_body: Live water levels: USGS Water Data API. Crossings: City of Austin and Travis County. Flood stages: NOAA National Weather Service. Map: OpenStreetMap.
onboarding.pledge.title: Before you start
onboarding.pledge.item1: I will never drive into water.
onboarding.pledge.item2: I will obey barricades and official warnings.
onboarding.pledge.item3: FordCast is an experimental prototype. It can be wrong or late, and it never tells me a road is safe.
onboarding.pledge.hint: Check all three statements to continue
onboarding.prototype: Check official crossing reports, available creek readings and nearby flood history. Archived storm demos are separate from current conditions. This prototype can be wrong or late.

storms.title: Learn from real floods
storms.body: Five real Austin storms rebuilt from USGS sensor records. Run one as a drill to see exactly what FordCast would have told you.
storms.blurb.halloween-2013: Overnight downpours sent Onion Creek to record levels. Homes flooded and crossings went under before dawn.
storms.blurb.memorial-day-2015: A holiday-weekend flood that swept through Hays and Travis counties. Barton and Onion Creeks rose fast.
storms.blurb.halloween-2015: Two years later, more than 10 inches of rain hit parts of the area in hours. Many crossings flooded at once.
storms.blurb.oct-2018: Heavy rain upstream in the Highland Lakes. A test of whether FordCast stays quiet when local creeks barely move.
storms.blurb.july-2025: A quick urban downpour. A test of fast rises that sensors may catch late · or not at all.
storms.track_body: Across {{storms}} past storms, FordCast's upstream-sensor rule warned “Avoid” before the downstream river sensor hit flood stage in {{hits}} of {{total}} cases · a median of {{lead}} minutes early. It missed {{missed}} and gave {{fa}} false alarm. It hasn't been checked against real road flooding yet, so never rely on it alone.
storms.track_note: Scored fairly: each storm is tested using settings learned only from the other storms.
lab.title: Science view
drive.ready_body: FordCast checks crossings ahead on your active route (or nearest to you) for official closures, weather warnings, and upstream sensor rises, reading updates out loud.
drive.tips: Tip: turn your volume up. Mount your phone · never hold it while driving.

explain.ffw: The National Weather Service has a Flash Flood Warning here. Low-water crossings can flood in minutes. Take another route.

explain.rain_history: Heavy rain is falling here, and flooding has been reported near this crossing before. Avoid it if you can.
explain.sensor_offline_rain: This crossing's sensor isn't reporting while heavy rain is falling. Treat it as flooded.
explain.heavy_rain: Heavy rain is falling nearby. Creeks can rise quickly. Watch for water over the road.

companion.title: Use with Google Maps
companion.body: Plan your trip in FordCast, then send suggested waypoints around reported hazards to Google Maps. Google Maps may choose a different road; check its route and obey official closures.
companion.guardian_on: On · FordCast runs in the background and warns you about a mile before a flooded or closed crossing, even while you navigate with Google Maps.
companion.guardian_off: Off · turn on to get warnings while you use Google Maps, Waze or Apple Maps.
companion.guardian_denied: Needs “Allow all the time” location permission. Change it in your phone’s Settings.
companion.expo_go: Guardian mode needs the installed FordCast app · Expo Go can't track location in the background. Route handoff to Google Maps works here.
companion.extension: On a computer, install the “FordCast for Google Maps” Chrome extension (extension folder in this project). It adds a FordCast panel to google.com/maps that flags closures and flooded crossings on your route and offers a route around them.
safety.title: Flood driving facts
safety.f1: Nearly half of flash-flood deaths happen in vehicles.
safety.f2: 12 inches of moving water can float most cars. 2 feet can carry away SUVs and trucks.
safety.f3: 6 inches of fast-moving water can knock an adult off their feet.
safety.f4: The road under the water may be washed out. You cannot see depth or damage, especially at night.
safety.f5: Never drive around a barricade. Turn around, don’t drown.
safety.source: Source: National Weather Service “Turn Around Don’t Drown”.

storms.impact_title: Why Low-Water Crossings Matter in Central Texas
storms.impact_body: Texas leads the nation in flood deaths, and over half of U.S. flash-flood fatalities happen inside vehicles. FordCast helps Central Texas drivers audit low-water crossings along their trip using official closures, NWS warnings, and transparent creek-gauge evidence.
physics.section: National Weather Service Flood Depth Guide
physics.title: What Moving Water Does to a Car
physics.subtitle: Select a water depth on the road to see National Weather Service Turn Around, Don't Drown® hazard thresholds.
physics.d6_sedan: Passenger cars: 6 inches of water reaches the bottom of most passenger cars, causing loss of control and possible stalling.
physics.d6_suv: Road visibility: Murky floodwater hides washed-out pavement, missing grates, or collapsed roadbeds beneath.
physics.d6_person: On foot: Just 6 inches of fast-moving water can knock an adult off their feet.
physics.d12_sedan: Passenger cars: A foot of moving water will float many vehicles, causing tires to lose traction and steering control.
physics.d12_suv: Crossovers & light trucks: Buoyancy lifts the chassis while moving current pushes the vehicle sideways toward the channel.
physics.d12_person: Extreme danger: Never attempt to walk or drive through 12 inches of moving floodwater.
physics.d24_sedan: All passenger vehicles: Swept downstream by moving floodwater.
physics.d24_suv: SUVs & pickups: Two feet of rushing water will carry away most vehicles, including SUVs and pickup trucks.
physics.d24_person: Life-threatening current: Over half of all flood-related drownings occur when a vehicle is driven into hazardous floodwater.
